body.hook: Two professional players can play the same solo with the same notes, and one makes the audience lean forward while the other doesn't. The difference is interpretation: the choices you make about what the music means and how to show it.

study.title: Make It Yours
study.question: How do musicians interpret a solo and prepare for an audition?
study.passage:
Part 1, Interpretive map (15 minutes): For your solo, mark: the overall character (for example "nostalgic," "playful"), each phrase's high point, places for rubato, colour changes (bright or dark tone), and the climax of the whole piece. Justify each choice with evidence from the score (harmony, range, markings) or the composer's style.
Part 2, Compare (10 minutes): Listen to two professional recordings of the same piece. Note two differences in interpretation. Which choices do you agree with?
Part 3, Audition prep (10 minutes): Typical audition: a prepared solo, scales, orchestral or band excerpts, and sight-reading. Make a two-week plan: daily scales, excerpt work slow to fast, solo run-throughs, weekly recording.
Part 4, Managing anxiety (10 minutes): Strategies: slow breathing (in 4, hold 4, out 6), a pre-performance routine, focusing on musical intentions rather than mistakes, positive self-talk, practising under pressure. Remember: some nerves give energy.
Part 5, Mock audition (15 minutes): Perform for a small panel of classmates who give one strength and one suggestion.
study.source: Original performance preparation task written for this lesson; anxiety strategies summarized from music performance psychology sources.

examples.title: Interpretation
examples.problem: A phrase rises to a high, held note marked "espressivo." What choice might you make?
examples.answer: Slight rubato into the high note and warmer tone at the peak
examples.explore: How would you return to tempo?

examples.title: Rubato
examples.problem: What is the danger of too much rubato?
examples.answer: The pulse is lost and the music sounds unsteady
examples.explore: How do you "steal" and "give back" time?

examples.title: Breathing
examples.problem: Use the breathing strategy before an audition.
examples.answer: Slow breathing calms the heart rate

examples.title: Excerpt
examples.problem: How should you practise a fast excerpt?
examples.answer: Start at 60% tempo with a metronome, increase gradually
